feedback.problem: At an archaeological site, an object is found with $30%$ of its original carbon-14 content. Given that the half-life of carbon-14 is $5\,730$ years, approximately how old is the object?
feedback.worked_solution:
The mass $M(t)$ of a radioactive substance at time $t$ can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
{M}^{′}(t)=-kM(t),\,M(0)={M}_{0}.
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
M(t)={M}_{0}{e}^{-kt}.
$$

The half-life ${t}_{1/2}$ is the time taken for the mass of the substance to reduce by one half and is given by

$$
{t}_{1/2}=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{k}.
$$

Since we know that ${t}_{1/2}=5\,730$ years, we have

$$
5\,730=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{k}\,⇒\,k=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{5\,730}.
$$

So, we have

$$
M(t)={M}_{0}{e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/5\,730}.
$$

We wish to calculate the time $t$ such that $M(t)=0.3{M}_{0}.$ So, we set up our equation as follows:

$$
0.3{M}_{0}={M}_{0}{e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/5\,730}
$$

Solving this equation for $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}0.3{M}_{0} & ={M}_{0}{e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/5\,730} \\ 0.3\cancel{{M}_{0}} & =\cancel{{M}_{0}}{e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/5\,730} \\ 0.3 & ={e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/5\,730} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.3) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-t\operatorname{ln}⁡2/5\,730}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.3) & =-\frac{t\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{5\,730} \\ t & =-\frac{5\,730\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.3)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ t & ≈9\,953\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the object is approximately $9\,953$ years old.
